The evidence shows sharply divided conclusions about whether organic food is better for the environment. Some sources argue organic farming reduces pollution, soil erosion, and energy use, and avoids synthetic pesticides, presenting it as environmentally beneficial [d3,d4,d6,d7]. Others counter that organic systems can be worse environmentally because they require substantially more land and do not clearly reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared with conventional systems [d5,d9,d11]. Several sources also note that organic farming permits certain persistent pesticides and alternative chemicals that harm soil and ecosystems over time, complicating any blanket claim of superiority [d1,d8]. Because the retrieved documents present mutually incompatible findings within the same scope and timeframe, there is no single consensus answer to whether organic food is “really” better for the environment.
